title: What if a Gen Z time-traveled to the Philippines in 1850?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: What if a Gen Z kid from twenty twenty-six woke up in the Philippines... in eighteen fifty?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Meet Migo. Nineteen years old. Phone at twelve percent. Ordering his third milk tea of the day.

lines.speaker: migo
lines.text: Ate, large, fifty percent sugar, extra pearls, please!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He blinks. And the whole world rewinds.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Binondo, Manila. The year is eighteen fifty.

lines.speaker: migo
lines.text: Okay. Is this, like, a cosplay event? Because the vibes are immaculate.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It's not cosplay. The Philippines has been a Spanish colony for almost three hundred years. And right now, the entire plaza is staring at his outfit.

lines.speaker: lola
lines.text: Ay, kawawa naman ang batang ito. Punit-punit ang pantalon!
lines.translation: Oh, you poor child. Your pants are all torn!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: To them, ripped jeans aren't fashion. They mean you're too poor to fix your pants.

lines.speaker: migo
lines.text: Lola, no! These cost three thousand pesos!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Problem number one: his phone. No signal. No WiFi. And no electricity. Manila won't switch on its first electric street lights until eighteen ninety-five.

lines.speaker: migo
lines.text: Forty-five years without a charger? I'm literally gonna die.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Problem number two: he speaks Taglish. The Tagalog part mostly works. The English part? Almost nobody here speaks English. The Americans won't arrive for another forty-eight years.

lines.speaker: migo
lines.text: Lodi! Sana all! No cap, this market is so aesthetic.

lines.speaker: vendor
lines.text: Ha? Ano raw?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: But there's good news. No milk tea, but there's tsokolate. Thick, hot chocolate, whipped with a wooden batirol. And fresh bibingka, baked on banana leaves.

lines.speaker: migo
lines.text: Wait. This actually slaps.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He tries to pay with GCash. The tindera just laughs. Here, money means silver coins.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then the cuadrilleros arrive. The town police. And they have questions.

lines.speaker: officer
lines.text: ¡Alto! ¿Cómo te llamas? ¿Y tu apellido?
lines.translation: Stop! What's your name? And your surname?

lines.speaker: migo
lines.text: Uh... Migo? Just Migo.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Wrong answer. Just months ago, Governor-General Clavería ordered families across the islands to take official surnames, from an alphabetical catalog.

lines.speaker: officer
lines.text: Desde hoy, te llamas... Migo Bautista.
lines.translation: From today, your name is... Migo Bautista.

lines.speaker: migo
lines.text: I got renamed... by a book?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And Migo is a healthy, nineteen year old man. Under Spanish rule, that means forty days of forced labor every year. It's called polo y servicio.

lines.speaker: migo
lines.text: Wait. So it's basically an unpaid internship?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The only way out is to pay a fee called the falla. Migo has zero money.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That night, Lola takes him in. And she teaches him the first rule of survival in eighteen fifty: always boil your water. Cholera has swept through Manila before, and it will again.

lines.speaker: lola
lines.text: Pakuluan mo muna ang tubig, anak.

lines.speaker: migo
lines.text: Lola, you're literally my only mutual here.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The next morning, Migo realizes he has one superpower. He knows the future.

lines.speaker: migo
lines.text: Okay, spoiler alert! In forty-eight years, you guys declare independence!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Rule number two: never shout independence in eighteen fifty. Especially not in front of a friar.

lines.speaker: friar
lines.text: ¿Qué dijiste, hijo?

lines.speaker: migo
lines.text: I said... I love pandesal! Haha.

lines.speaker: migo
lines.text: Wait. Where's Rizal? I need to meet Rizal.

lines.speaker: kid
lines.text: Sino si Rizal?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: José Rizal won't even be born for another eleven years.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Day three. Migo has a new surname, a lola, and a serious tsokolate addiction. Then, his dead phone lights up. One percent. A way back home.

lines.speaker: migo
lines.text: Okay... do I go back to twenty twenty-six? Or stay for the bibingka?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Would you go back, or stay in eighteen fifty? Tell me in the comments.
